title: Why Does the Moon Change Shape? Explained in 60 Seconds
description: Some nights the Moon is a perfect circle, other nights it is a thin sliver. Here is the simple reason behind the Moon's phases.
tags: why does the moon change shape

scenes.on_screen: Why does the Moon change shape?
scenes.text: Some nights the Moon is a perfect circle. Other nights it is just a thin silver curve. But does the Moon really grow and shrink? Let's find out.

scenes.on_screen: The Moon has no light of its own
scenes.text: Here is the first secret. The Moon does not make any light. What we see is sunlight bouncing off its surface and travelling back to our eyes.
At any moment, the half of the Moon facing the Sun is lit up. As the Moon travels around the Earth, we simply see more or less of that bright half.
When the bright side faces us, we get a full moon. When it faces away, we get a new moon. In between, we see crescents and half moons.
The whole cycle takes about twenty nine and a half days. If you enjoyed this, subscribe for more quick science explained simply.
